tasks.title: Reseat the driver tests at the argv seam
tasks.goal: Add a run_driver(action, brief) helper that writes TALLY_BRIEF, execs the driver binary, and parses TALLY_FINAL_MESSAGE=; migrate the 49 action-only tests onto it; add coverage for main(), load_brief(), emit(), and the DriverError-to-exit-1 path, none of which is tested today. This converts the port from a month to a week and is worth doing on its own merits (Decision D36).
deliveredBehaviors: The production entrypoint has test coverage

tasks.title: New spec-build-driver crate behind the same seam
tasks.goal: Create the spec-build-driver crate in the workspace, compiled to its own binary, behind the exact argv seam (TALLY_BRIEF in, one TALLY_FINAL_MESSAGE= line out, DriverError to stderr + exit 1), separately pinned: the registry keeps modeling flow and driver as two store paths (campaign_registry.rs 1325-1326); never folded into the tally CLI. It imports campaign_contract directly -- no mirror.
deliveredBehaviors: A Rust driver binary answers the worklist action end to end
Flow and driver remain independently pinned

acceptanceCriteria.description: The crate builds and its worklist action round-trips a fixture brief.

tasks.title: Port campaign_worktrees with the driver
tasks.goal: Port campaign_worktrees.py (638 LOC: flock lane preparation locking, git-config identity round-trip, add/resume/remove/prune, change_set_fingerprint) into the driver crate. Never ported first (Decision D35); the flock-interleaving lane-serialization property gets a Rust test equivalent.
deliveredBehaviors: Lane-cut serialization is proven in Rust

tasks.title: Port the surviving driver actions
tasks.goal: Port the ~6,700 surviving lines: the pure fold half (reconcile, pardon arithmetic, gate normalization/enforcement, canonical decoders -- where the type system pays) and the effectful half (git choreography via std::process::Command, distinguishing ref-absent from command-failed). The reseated Python suite runs against the Rust binary during the port as the migration oracle; parity on the full suite is the exit criterion.
deliveredBehaviors: The Rust driver passes the reseated suite
Python and Rust drivers are behaviorally identical at the seam

acceptanceCriteria.description: The reseated suite passes against the Rust binary.

tasks.title: Single-source the spec-build.js argsSchema from Rust
tasks.goal: Generate or golden-verify the spec-build.js inline argsSchema (the second and larger hand-copy, examples/flows/spec-build.js 141-249) from the Rust contract, in the direction #520 names, so the JS copy can never skew. With the Python mirror deleted next task, contract copies go from four toward one (Rust authority) plus the nix module (Chapter P territory).
deliveredBehaviors: The JS argsSchema cannot drift from the Rust contract

tasks.title: Delete Python and the corpus machinery (victory lap)
tasks.goal: Delete drivers/spec_build_driver.py, drivers/campaign_worktrees.py, the contract-corpus generator (campaign_contract_corpus.rs emitter), the Python byte-compare decoder test, and the regex that re-parses Rust source -- the verification scaffolding that existed solely to keep Python honest. Flag agency_nightly_driver.py explicitly: it rides the same port or is grandfathered by name in the chapter record, never by silence. Update the flake stdlib-only check scope accordingly.
deliveredBehaviors: Zero Python in the campaign path
One contract source with one generated JS golden
